vedic_reference.note: Virbhadra is the name of a king in the Mahabharata who was a powerful warrior and the father of Bhishma Pitamaha. He was a descendant of the lunar dynasty and ruled over the kingdom of Hastinapur. Virbhadra is also known as Vibhishana and is considered to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

data.cultural_impact: Virbhadra is a central figure in Hindu mythology, revered particularly in the Himachal Pradesh region of India. He is depicted as a fierce warrior god with multiple arms, holding weapons, and a fiery_{(aj_)_} appearance. The Shaivite tradition invokes Virbhadra during rituals to invoke the destructive power of Lord Shiva. There are numerous temples dedicated to Virbhadra, situated in beautiful mountainous regions, where he is worshipped with great devotion and fervor.
data.spiritual_significance: Virbhadra represents the aspect of Lord Shiva that embodies fearlessness and destruction of evil. He is a reminder to believers that fearlessness is a crucial trait to possess, especially when battling inner demons or facing external adversities. Furthermore, he symbolizes the divine power to eliminate negativity and restore balance and harmony in the universe. Worship of Virbhadra is thought to provide protection against fear, anger, and negative energies.
